system_prompt_style.evidence_quote: Agents are specific in-stances of the LLM, each equipped with unique system prompts that guide their behavior.
system_prompt_style.note: Prompt differs per agent (Base/Error/Form) and form state; each is a template with {datetime}, {error}, {information_to_collect} (paper Table 2). Prompt-building code not in bundle.

env_context_strategy.evidence_quote: The user's input and conversation history are injected into a prompt template to create the final input for the model.
env_context_strategy.note: Chatbot domain, no repository/environment context; tools are Google/search/code interpreter.

observation_format.evidence_quote: executes it, returning the result to the LLM

tool_call_format.note: Parser/agent construction code (converso package) not in bundle; paper mentions formatting errors for structured outputs only.

tool_count.note: Tool registration code not in bundle; paper lists 6 Personal Assistant tools (PythonCodeInterpreter, GoogleSearch, GmailRetriever, GoogleCalendarRetriever, GoogleCalendarCreator, GmailSender) but default registry not seen.

edit_primitive.evidence_quote: What distinguishes different use cases in the Converso framework is the definition of the tools to use for the specific application
edit_primitive.note: No file-editing tool among listed tools; value list designed for SWE harnesses.

tool_schema_source.note: Tool definition files not in bundle; FormTools are BaseTool subclasses with args_schema (likely auto_generated via Pydantic).

protocol_standardization.note: No dependency file contents in bundle to grep.

loop_primitives.evidence_quote: This flow is constructed as a graph using LangGraph
loop_primitives.note: Model requests tool execution, results fed back; RabbitMQ message-driven processing (Sec. 3.1).

planning_granularity.evidence_quote: FormTools maintain an internal state that tracks the progress of the data collection process.
planning_granularity.note: Form state is structured but not a plan.

multi_agent_topology.evidence_quote: The Base Agent is responsible for conducting the conver-sation with the user, while the Error Agent assists by correcting any errors
multi_agent_topology.note: Paper calls it multi-agent, but Base/Error/Form agents are prompt variants of one LLM swapped by the graph; closest to single (could be read as pipeline/role handoff).

delegation_mechanism.evidence_quote: the Base Agent is replaced by the Form Agent

human_in_loop.evidence_quote: the user is presented with a summary of the collected information for confirmation

long_term_memory.note: Redis persists per-chat state, which is continuation not long-term memory; no memory registry in bundle.

self_verification.note: Error Agent corrects format errors (step-level); form validation is input validation. No verification code in bundle.

retry_policy.note: Error Agent requery is step-level, not task retry.

termination_condition.evidence_quote: The max-imum number of iterations is set to 25.
termination_condition.note: Final answer ends flow (Sec. 3.2); 25 is evaluation setting.

execution_isolation.evidence_quote: All components of the Converso chatbot are created as Docker containers orchestrated by Kubernetes.
execution_isolation.note: PythonCodeInterpreter isolation not shown; default run is docker compose.

permission_model.note: Per-form confirmation step exists (Sec. 3.3) but permission code not in bundle.

tracing.note: README asks for LangChain API key (LangSmith tracing likely) but config not in bundle.

eval_hooks.note: File tree; paper Sec. 4.2 evaluation protocol with user simulator.

target_domain.evidence_quote: The framework for goal-oriented LLM conversations
target_domain.note: Conversational chatbot/form filling; could be other.

model_agnostic.note: model_factory.py not in bundle; paper says LLM selectable, evaluated with gpt-3.5-turbo.

primary_artifact.evidence_quote:
Source code for the paper Converso: Improving LLM Chatbot Interfaces and Task
Execution via Conversational Forms.
